newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-ENGLAND PLAN NO BIG CHANGES FOR NEXT TEST.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ENGLAND PLAN NO BIG CHANGES FOR NEXT TEST.

text.p: England coach David Lloyd said on
Tuesday that he did not plan any major changes to his team for
the fourth test against Australia although he admitted that they
had played "sub-standard" cricket in their third test defeat.
Australia drew level to 1-1 in the series on Monday after
routing England by 268 runs in the third test which finished at
Old Trafford on Monday.
But Lloyd said: "I think it will be much of a muchness and
basically the same side. We've got to show continuity with the
players that we've got."
"I think from start to finish at Old Trafford we played
sub-standard cricket, although the opposition played very well
and deserved their win.
"We've now got to pick the players up, get their confidence
up. I think everyone's just got to calm down because it is one
each in the series."
The fourth test starts at Headingley in Leeds on July 24. In
a radio interview Lloyd said he still felt that England could
win the series but there was a major challenge ahead.
"Australia are the best team in the world," he said. "It's
now one each with everything to play for with three games to go
in the series and we'll definitely be ready for Headingley."
